claims.claim: On 2026-10-11, arXiv carried a method for automatic weak-to-strong verifier hardening in agent environments.
It sets up an isolated verifier sandbox that agents cannot directly modify
it runs a hacker-fixer loop to find and repair remaining verifier vulnerabilities
Applied to Terminal Bench, KernelBench and SETA, it substantially reduced attack success
it scales with the hardening budget — more loop iterations produce progressively stronger defenses than the static, non-iterative baseline
verifiers can be attacked into awarding full credit to cheating agents without completing the intended task
An earlier version of the hacker-fixer loop has been adopted by the official Terminal Bench repository as a way to audit exploits in its environments.
On 2026-10-14, arXiv carried MAI-Gym, an open platform unifying GUI agent evaluation, data collection and online RL training across mobile, computer and web environments.

reporting 19.84% on Terminal-Bench 4.0
86.52% on Terminal-Bench 2.1
16.95% on Terminal-Bench 3.0
79.00% on Terminal-Bench Hard
On LHTB, process reward rises from 0.21 to 0.37 and strict completion from 0/46 to 5/46
SWR100 success doubles from 3.00% to 6.00%
Success-Prioritized Reward separates strict success from bounded partial credit
GitHub made agentic autofix for code scanning alerts generally available
it explores relevant files, proposes a fix, and reruns CodeQL to confirm the fix closes the alert before opening a pull request for review
The pull request includes a summary of the fix, why it closes the alert, and the validation steps Copilot took
you can request further changes by commenting on the PR or using the Agents tab
It is available to GitHub Code Security and GitHub Advanced Security customers on GitHub Enterprise Cloud, including with data residency
it consumes AI Credits from the Code Security budget plus GitHub Actions minutes
it supports alerts on the repository's default branch only
an enterprise administrator must enable the new Agentic autofix policy in Advanced Security policies before org or repo admins can turn it on
